text: Kazuki. Chapter 3. The night the sun went dark. Previously,
Yorichi found a home with Uta. They were expecting a child. He left to seek a midwife,
but stopped to help a grieving stranger when he returned no one answered.
His hand rests against the door. Uta? The room beyond is still.
Yorichi steps inside. A moment ago, he was a husband coming home. Now, he cannot make himself
take another step. Uta and their unborn child are gone. A demon has taken the life they were
building together. The hearth has grown cold. Yorichi kneels beside her. There is no enemy left
for him to face. Only the silence. I said I would come back. The words leave him softly.
He remembers her in the doorway, waiting for his return. His hands can no longer change what
happened in this room. Days pass. Light crosses the floor and disappears. Yorichi remains beside Uta,
unable to say farewell. Outside, the world continues. Inside, he cannot imagine a morning that
belongs to him. At last, a traveling demon slayer finds the house. He sees the grieving man inside
and kneels a short distance away. After a long silence, he speaks gently. We should lay them to rest.
Together, they prepare a grave. Earth falls beneath Yorichi's hands. He has carried water
to this house, gathered wood for its hearth, and imagined his child growing here. Now, he must
leave them beneath the earth. At the grave, he takes out the small wooden flute his brother made.
It rests within his palm worn by years of keeping. He closes his fingers around it.
The things he loves have never needed to be grand.
The demon slayer tells him of others who stand between demons and the sleeping world.
Yorichi listens. Until now, his extraordinary strength had seemed unnecessary to the life he wanted.
He asks where he should go.
He gathers his few belongings. The little flute goes safely inside his clothing.
At the doorway, he looks back once. He cannot promise to return to the life he knew. He can still
choose what he does next. Among the demon slayers, Yorichi watches the movement of a sword. His
eyes follow the breathing, the shift of weight, the instant before a strike. The gift he once
feared using has found a terrible purpose. He could not save the home he loved.
Beyond these mountains, other doors are waiting for someone to return.
Yorichi lifts the practice sword to be continued.
